opening.argument: The video is plainly structured as an instructional Intel RAID setup guide, walking viewers through technical configuration from start to finish. It gives concrete operating steps, including selecting RAID in SATA mode, and shows both the Intel Rapid Storage Technology volume-creation menu and the Windows installation disk-selection screen. The speaker also gives a material caution that creating a RAID volume wipes all data on the drives. Although the tutorial includes ordinary requests to subscribe, like, dislike, or comment, those engagement prompts do not transform the technical demonstration into a deceptive offer. The sponsored SSD disclosure is likewise presented in the demonstration context, while the RAID warning makes the relevant operational risk explicit.

citations.quote: So the SATA mode selection is usually IDE, AHCI and RAID. So that should be pretty self explanatory. Go with Raid.
In fact, when you create a RAID volume, you wipe out all the data on those drives.
